The Linux Foundation is a 501(c)(6) non-profit that provides a neutral, trusted hub for developers and organizations to code, manage, and scale open technology projects and ecosystems.

 - Permissionless nature leads to fragmentation of meaning

 - Decentralization leads to too many standards https://xkcd.com/927/

 - Immutability leads to exponential data + query infrastructure complexity

 - Neutrality means that no one is accountable for interpretations

Blockchain data is public. It is not usable at institutional scale. Despite being open, blockchain data is fragmented, hard to interpret, and painful to maintain. Even a simple question like “Who are the largest Ethereum token holders over time?” can require running nodes, ingesting full chain history, decoding contracts, cleaning edge cases, and writing complex SQL.




BLOCKCHAINS ARE OPTIMIZED FOR WRITES, NOT READS. 

They are built for consensus and execution, not searchability, standardization, or financial interpretation. Blockchains are computers, not databases https://x.com/Tim_Roughgarden/status/1512847113599729668. Every protocol defines its own schema. The same economic action can be encoded in dozens of different ways. The result:

 - Fragmented standards

 - Exponential complexity

 - No accountability for interpretation

 - Events without economic meaning

Finance cannot operate on that, it needs an effective system of record.

 - Semantic Gap: Translating raw events into financial concepts like payments, trades, deposits, and staking income

 - Standardization Gap: Mapping thousands of protocols into a single canonical cross chain schema

 - Infrastructure Gap: Read optimized, globally distributed data at web scale

 - Accountability Gap: Auditable methodology, SLAs, and SOC 1 and 2 compliance

The result is a neutral, canonical data layer institutions can build on with confidence.




FINANCE IS MOVING ONCHAIN

Apnimed is committed to innovation, as well as state-of-the-art advancements in sleep medicine, which is leading to the development of a portfolio of novel pharmacologic therapies for sleep apnea and related disorders.

The Director, Oracle Financials & Platform Engineering is a technically deep leader at the intersection of business and technology who sets the strategy for the organization's Oracle platforms. Under the shared ownership operating model for Oracle ERP and EPM, this role is the designated technical owner of the Oracle Cloud financial applications suite: it owns the platform, integrations, security, technical controls, and environments, while Finance owns business processes, functional configuration, and business outcomes.

The role leads and grows the enterprise Oracle team across Financials engineering, integration, and database administration for Oracle Financials and other Oracle applications, with Oracle ERP and EPM as the primary focus. * Set the Oracle technical strategy and multi-year roadmap across Oracle ERP, EPM, integration, and database platforms, aligned with Finance, enterprise data, and enterprise architecture priorities.
* Serve as the designated technical owner for the Oracle financials platform (e.g., ERP, EPM) and a trusted partner to the Finance leadership, co-owning governance, including the RACI, change approvals for configuration, releases, security, and integrations.
* Act as a key stakeholder in Oracle licensing, contract, and investment decisions, providing usage, cost, and technical analysis, and own the strategic technical relationship with Oracle and implementation partners.
* Own technical administration of Oracle Cloud ERP Financials and related applications, and the technical layer of Oracle EPM (e.g., EPBCS, FCCS, ARCS, Narrative Reporting, EDM). Finance owns business processes (close, planning design), functional configuration, and business outcomes.
* Ensure business requirements from Finance Systems and super users are translated into technical designs that favor standard Oracle capabilities, extending with Visual Builder, Redwood, and OCI only within enterprise architecture standards.

**Job Description Summary**
===========================

As part of the GE Aerospace Digital Technology organization supporting the Defense & Systems (D&S) business, the Director of DevOps, Support, and Operations keeps the Defense and Systems Customer Experience (DSCX) application portfolio secure, reliable, and compliant. This is a people-leadership role accountable for vulnerability remediation, reliability (SLA, SLO, and SLI), automation and toil reduction, vendor management, defect management, legacy lifecycle and sunsetting, and resilience and continuity including on-call and disaster recovery. This person will lead a team of operations and application engineers and set the operational discipline for the portfolio.

**Job Description**
===================

**Why This Role Exists**

DSCX owns 30+ digital products for Defense & Systems. Today our technical product managers wear three hats for their products: product management, project management, and operations. We are dividing that load across three dedicated functions, and this role will build out the operations discipline, consolidating ticket management, software hygiene, patching, and vulnerability closure into a single team. This role is planned to have 6-8 direct reports, and the portfolio includes many legacy applications and reports that need to be retired, rewritten, or absorbed into our AI product vision. Vulnerability and high priority defect findings come from the Defense & Systems security organization under the BISO, and closing them inside the severity SLA, including CMMC obligations on affected products, is part of this team's accountability. Your charge is to standardize processes and artifacts, build automation that removes the manual work, and then coach and train your team to hold it. You should be experienced with AI and know where it creates opportunity to expand what the team can deliver.

**Environment**

The DSCX portfolio runs primarily on AWS, Palantir Foundry, or through SaaS based 3rd party solutions, with on-premise implementations supported for customers whose data sensitivity requires it. Delivery runs through Rally and Microsoft Teams and ServiceNow is our system of record for incident, change, and defect management. Monitoring and alerting tooling varies by application across the portfolio, and consolidating it is part of this team's work. Finally, the portfolio carries a $25+MM annual budget across our product line.

**Roles and Responsibilities**  
  
**Security and Vulnerability Remediation**

* Own vulnerability remediation and high-priority application defects across the DSCX portfolio, working against the policy, scanning cadence, and severity SLAs set by the Defense & Systems Business Information Security Officer (BISO), who is the source for both.
* Accountable for getting DSCX applications compliant against the BISO's D&S-wide program, including CMMC obligations on affected products.
* Own the remediation backlog with a named owner and target date

The Vice President of Technology provides strategic leadership for Biltmore's enterprise technology, digital guest experience, data capabilities, and artificial intelligence initiatives. NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

At NVIDIA, we are building an advanced AI-native autonomous driving architecture. It integrates traditional safety-focused autonomous systems, fully learned driving approaches, foundation models, world models, and scalable AI systems into one production platform. Autonomous driving is entering a new era. The next generation of AV systems will not be purely classical robotics stacks, nor purely end-to-end neural networks. We believe the future lies in deeply integrating the strengths of classical, interpretable safety architectures with large-scale learning-based systems. We seek a Director-level technical leader who can define this architecture and build a world-class engineering organization. They will lead the team and drive technology from research and prototypes through production and scale. This leader will work across classical autonomy and modern AI. They will bring together teams and technologies in prediction, planning, control, safety, end-to-end driving, large-scale pre-trained models, and embodied AI. If you want to build the architecture that could define autonomous systems for the next decade, this is the place.

NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

NVIDIA’s advanced datacenter boards push forward chip packaging, PCB fabrication, SMT, assembly, and testing capabilities. Dedicated teams take responsibility for each technology: packaging manages the package, PCB and materials handle fabrication and stack-up, SMT and assembly oversee build processes, and test and SI focus on test capabilities. The challenge is to align these improvements across the stack—from chip to PCB, PCB to SMT, SMT to assembly, and assembly to test. Each domain’s innovation delivers maximum benefit when downstream consequences are considered early. The Senior Director, Board PDE oversees integration methods that make this possible—coordinating handoffs, engineering cross-domain effects before changes, and optimizing the entire chain.

- Design, implement, and institutionalize the integration readiness process for all next-generation datacenter board products — owning manufacturing and test readiness end to end so build starts land on schedule and at target yield.
- Guide the functional teams in developing cross-boundary techniques before silicon and stackup freeze occurs. Focus on warpage-tolerant DFM and reflow for next-gen BGA pitch. Manage impedance and CTE control for high-speed stackups. Lock pad-map and fab methods at an early stage.
- Build, lead, and develop a global Board PDE organization across three technical pillars — PCB & Fab, SMT/PCBA, and High-Speed Connector & Signal Integrity.
- Set up integration oversight throughout the chip-to-board stack. Define entry and exit requirements at each domain boundary. Lead the gates to confirm one qualified domain is ready to pass to the next.
- Collaborate with Operations Test Engineering and Signal Integrity to establish test coverage and manufacturing test flow requirements, applying that thoroughness to the tester and diagnostic boards.
- Take charge of reliability and yield performance throughout the stack. Investigate excursions to identify root causes. Address DFx and alternate-component gaps with the factory planning and design teams.

Our mission is to return the atmosphere to 280 ppm CO₂. We convert excess inedible biomass into carbon-rich bio-oil and inject it into underground storage for permanent carbon removal. At scale, we can use bio-oil to make fossil-free iron.
 
Our carbon removal efforts began in 2020 with initial purchases from customers like Stripe, Shopify, and Microsoft. Since then, we’ve scaled to thousands of tons of carbon removal, grown to over a hundred employees, and established three locations in San Francisco, Colorado, and Louisiana.

Who is NTE, NTE 35W, and LBJ?

The North Tarrant Express (NTE) was the first design-build-finance-operate-maintain managed lanes project in Texas and consisted of the complete reconstruction of 13.3 miles of the existing I-820/SH-183 corridor between Dallas and Fort Worth. Since opening in October 2014, nine months ahead of the contracted completion date, the general highway lanes are experiencing a 70% decrease in congestion time and a 15% increase in average speed. This Cintra-led project has doubled capacity and significantly improved mobility along this heavily congested corridor that traverses the heart of six cities through Northeast Tarrant County.

The North Tarrant Express 35W (NTE 35W) project spans 16.8 miles from I-30 in downtown Fort Worth to Eagle Parkway at the north end of Alliance Airport. The project is operated and maintained by the Cintra-led consortium in North Texas. This project has improved mobility by adding additional road capacity through a combination of general highway lanes and continuous frontage roads, along with tolled express lanes that use variable pricing to keep traffic moving.

The LBJ Express (LBJ) is currently the largest P3 operation in Texas and one of the largest ever undertaken in the U.S. It is a regionally-significant transportation improvement project in North Texas that is relieving severe congestion in the dense urban area of north Dallas. In 2009, the Cintra-led consortium was selected to complete the design, construction, finance, operation, and maintenance of the project along I-635 and I-35E. Since opening in September 2015, the general highway lanes are realizing a 60% decrease in congestion time and a 10% increase in average speed.

ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD
  
  
The Campaign Finance Board is a nonpartisan, independent city agency that empowers New Yorkers to have a greater impact on their elections. Our mission is to make local democracy more open, transparent, and equitable by removing barriers to participation.
  
  
We make it easier for New Yorkers to vote, meaningfully support candidates for city office, and run for office themselves. NYC Votes, our voter engagement initiative, meets people where they are to share trustworthy election information and help New Yorkers make a plan to vote. We publish the citywide Voter Guide, which delivers information about candidates directly to voters’ doors. Our public matching funds program ensures small contributions can make a big difference, allowing regular people to run for office by relying on the support of other regular people, not just wealthy donors and special interests. And we lift the veil on how candidates raise and spend money, increasing transparency and accountability in local government.
  
  
We believe that when every New Yorker is empowered to participate meaningfully in elections, candidates will better reflect the communities they serve, elected leaders will be more accountable to the public, and New Yorkers will have a democracy they can truly trust.

The new Data department will ensure that the agency’s information is trustworthy, well governed, protected, and ready to use. **Job Summary**:

The Director of Quality Assurance leads the QA organization through its transformation to an AI-optimized SDLC, able to support multiple product launches and continuous feature delivery in parallel across a multi-tenant SaaS platform. This leader defines the overarching quality strategy, champions the integration of AI tools across the entire SDLC, and scales automated, resilient testing frameworks to accelerate delivery while sustaining the reliability and regulatory compliance Medrio's customers depend on. This position reports directly to the SVP of Engineering and works closely with Development, Product, Support, and Compliance throughout the SDLC. The QA organization is geographically dispersed, combining onshore and offshore teams of in-house engineers and external vendor partners working across multiple time zones.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* **AI-Driven Quality Strategy:** Lead the strategic integration of generative and predictive AI tools throughout the SDLC, including AI-assisted test case creation, requirements analysis, and automated risk-based test coverage.
* **Quality Throughput & Capacity:** Scale quality output in line with an AI-accelerated development organization, ensuring test capacity keeps pace with development output without compromising quality. Success is measured through cycle time to release, escaped defect rate, automated test coverage, and full regression suite runtime.
* **Modern Test Automation Leadership:** Oversee the evolution of automated testing strategies for a multi-tenant SaaS platform, prioritizing modern frameworks like Playwright alongside AI-powered self-healing test infrastructure to minimize script maintenance and maximize suite reliability. This includes tenant isolation and data-segregation testing, configuration-driven test matrices across tenant variants, and management of shared-schema regression risk.
* **Organization Oversight:** Direct all activities of the QA organization, ensuring continuous validation, high platform stability, and alignment with modern quality engineering best practices.
* **Regulatory & Compliance Quality:** Ensure QA practices, documentation, and evidence meet the requirements of a regulated healthcare environment (including HIPAA, 21 CFR Part 11, GxP/CSV, SOC 2, and GDPR where applicable), and support internal and customer audits as a senior representative of the quality function.
* **Validation of AI-Generated Test Assets:** Own the framework by which AI-assisted test artifacts are reviewed, approved, and evidenced, ensuring automation generated with AI meets the traceability and audit standards required in a validated environment.
* **Security-Forward Quality:** Partner with Security and DevOps to embed security testing into the delivery pipeline (SAST/DAST, dependency and vulnerability triage, and coordination of penetration testing), and ensure PHI is appropriately handled and de-identified across test environments and test data.

Karman is a fast-growing NVIDIA-backed AI company enabling AI data centers to dynamically orchestrate power and unlock more compute capacity from existing energy infrastructure. For over a decade, we have applied AI to the electric grid, bringing real-time visibility and power-flow control to complex energy infrastructure. Our Karman platform, built on a custom NVIDIA module, brings that same capability to AI data centers, giving operators a way to better use the power already available to them.  
  
**The team**  
The Power Applications team takes power orchestration algorithms from idea to production. We develop, ship, and maintain the applications that run on Karman to solve power management problems and orchestrate control actions in real time in megawatt-scale data centers. We own the decision layer of Karman’s real-time control loop: turning live power telemetry into power management commands fast enough to keep data centers safe and fully utilized.  
  
Our scope requires us to blend research and development with continuous delivery. The team is a mix of data scientists, algorithms engineers, software engineers, and AI infrastructure engineers, organized into two complementary groups. Research and development proves and matures new control, estimation, and forecasting capabilities and builds the evidence to decide what moves into the product. Continuous delivery turns that validated theory into reliable, deployable software and keeps it performing in the field.  
  
**The role**  
The Director, Power Applications leads this team and owns its outcomes on both workflows, reporting to the VP of AI and Applications.  
  
The job sits at the interface between research and implementation. On one side you lead scientists and senior algorithms engineers working on open problems, where the hardest questions are how to interpret, prioritize, and resource work with ambiguous scope, and when to pivot, double down, or shelve. On the other side you lead principal-level software engineers shipping control software with hard reliability guarantees against committed product dates. Your job is to make those two sides one program: research framed so that it produces decisions on time, results that move into production as deliberate increments, and field performance that feeds the next research question.  
  
You are also the team's single point of contact for planning and reporting. You partner with Product and technical program management on roadmap commitments, keep the technical roadmap visible alongside the product roadmap, and make the trade-offs between delivery, research, and requests for proof points and demonstrations explicit, with their costs stated. The Opportunity
Philanthropy has long operated with fragmented data, duplicative processes, and systems that do not easily speak to one another. The Philanthropy Data Commons (PDC) was created to change that.

By enabling information to move securely across the systems that organizations already use, the PDC can reduce the repetitive administrative burden on nonprofits, help changemakers gain greater visibility to aligned funders, and give them greater control over how their information is shared, while giving funders a clearer view of organizations, needs, and funding flows.

The PDC has moved well beyond an idea. With significant foundational work completed, including a live Exchange application, an evolving governance framework, a growing network of funders and ecosystem participants, and more than 20 organizations committed to sharing data, PDC is entering an important period of transition and growth.

The focus now is on expanding participation, demonstrating the value of shared data at greater scale, and building the coalition that can make PDC an enduring part of how philanthropy works.

The inaugural Executive Director will have a rare chance to help shape the next stage of the initiative and a broader shift in the field. They will build on significant investment and momentum while helping the PDC grow its reach, deepen its partnerships, strengthen its financial sustainability, and establish its long-term organizational home.

At a time when advances in AI are making access to trusted, well-governed data increasingly important, the PDC has the potential to become essential infrastructure for a more connected, informed, and effective philanthropic sector. For an entrepreneurial leader energized by building in ambiguity, this is a chance to take years of investment and a powerful sector-wide idea and turn it into something enduring, shaping not only the future of the PDC but how philanthropy shares and uses data.

About the Philanthropy Data Commons
Conceptualized in 2021, the Philanthropy Data Commons is a collaborative initiative temporarily hosted by Mac Services, Inc. that connects the systems, organizations, and data that philanthropy runs on. It provides a shared infrastructure that allows funders, changemakers, and the ecosystem partners they already use to share information on their own terms.

The Director, Risk Adjustment Product & Technology will lead the product roadmap, and technology capabilities that enable Mosaic Health to identify, prioritize, orchestrate, and capture burden-of-illness opportunities across its patient populations.

This role will own the evolution of Mosaic’s enterprise Burden of Illness (BOI) Hub—the centralized intelligence and orchestration layer that brings together clinical, claims, payer, attribution, and supplemental data to determine which patients and clinical opportunities should be acted upon, through which intervention, and at what point in the workflow.

- Own the product vision, strategy, roadmap, and operating model for Mosaic’s enterprise risk adjustment technology capabilities.

- enterprise-owned decisioning and prioritization,

- execution engines,

- enterprise performance analytics.

As AI accelerates software development, the need for reliable verification is only increasing. Antithesis exists to solve that problem.

About Amazon Web Services

Amazon Web Services (AWS) offers a broad set of global compute, storage, database, analytics, application, and deployment services that help organizations move faster, lower IT costs, and scale applications. These services are trusted by the largest enterprises and the hottest start-ups to power a wide variety of workloads — including web and mobile applications, data processing and warehousing, storage, archive, and many others.

AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

The Opportunity

For a decade, WorkSpaces has been exceptional at what it was designed to do: securely deliver a virtual desktop where a user logs in, applications load, work happens, the session ends. It is reactive by design—with no memory of what occurred, no understanding of intent, and no ability to act on the user's behalf. But work has changed. The modern enterprise now runs on three workforces: humans who set direction, AI agents that execute delegated work, and the systems that run the business. Non-human identities already outnumber human ones, yet no infrastructure layer governs all three within a single trust boundary. Whoever solves this—making the secure, governed path the fastest path—will define how the world works for the next decade.

Amazon WorkSpaces is uniquely positioned to lead this transformation. We are extending its trust boundary from humans to humans and AI agents working together, governed by default. This is not an incremental improvement but a reimagining of the workspace itself—from a platform that delivers applications and compute into one that actively partners with users: understanding intent, orchestrating workflows across systems, anticipating needs, and reducing friction at every step.

We are looking for a seasoned product leader to own the end-to-end product strategy for Amazon WorkSpaces and define the future of work at the intersection of human talent and agentic AI. You will treat the workspace not as a container for compute but as the orchestration layer where humans and AI collaborate—reimagining every surface through the lens of human-AI partnership, and making AI adoption effortless for enterprises that have rightly prioritized security, governance, and compliance above all else.

Key job responsibilities

- Define and evangelize the product vision for Agentic WorkSpaces—the enterprise platform where humans and AI age

PsiQuantum's mission is to build the first useful quantum computers: machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries.

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry, including partners like GlobalFoundries, we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don't feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.

That approach has since been tested at the highest level of scrutiny the U.S. government applies to emerging technology, and it has held up. In 2025, PsiQuantum closed a $1 billion funding round that valued the company at $7 billion. In 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce signed a $100 million Letter of Intent under the CHIPS and Science Act, followed by a $125 million agreement with DARPA under Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, PsiQuantum's most valuable U.S. government agreement to date. This year, we also broke ground on our utility-scale quantum computer in Brisbane, Australia, and continued building out our Chicago site. Victor Peng, our CEO, and co-founder Jeremy O'Brien, now Executive Chairman, lead a team and board that reflects how seriously the world is taking this build, joined this year by Intel's Lip-Bu Tan and Atomico's Niklas Zennström.

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies, including Airbus, Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical, to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact.

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift, and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we now have the funding, the government validation, and the sites under construction to make it real.

About Amazon Web Services
  
  
Amazon Web Services (AWS) offers a broad set of global compute, storage, database, analytics, application, and deployment services that help organizations move faster, lower IT costs, and scale applications. These services are trusted by the largest enterprises and the hottest start-ups to power a wide variety of workloads — including web and mobile applications, data processing and warehousing, storage, archive, and many others.
  
  
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.  
  
The Opportunity
  
  
For a decade, WorkSpaces has been exceptional at what it was designed to do: securely deliver a virtual desktop where a user logs in, applications load, work happens, the session ends. It is reactive by design—with no memory of what occurred, no understanding of intent, and no ability to act on the user's behalf. But work has changed. The modern enterprise now runs on three workforces: humans who set direction, AI agents that execute delegated work, and the systems that run the business. Non-human identities already outnumber human ones, yet no infrastructure layer governs all three within a single trust boundary. Whoever solves this—making the secure, governed path the fastest path—will define how the world works for the next decade.
  
  
Amazon WorkSpaces is uniquely positioned to lead this transformation. We are extending its trust boundary from humans to humans and AI agents working together, governed by default. This is not an incremental improvement but a reimagining of the workspace itself—from a platform that delivers applications and compute into one that actively partners with users: understanding intent, orchestrating workflows across systems, anticipating needs, and reducing friction at every step.
  
  
We are looking for a seasoned product leader to own the end-to-end product strategy for Amazon WorkSpaces and define the future of work at the intersection of human talent and agentic AI. You will treat the workspace not as a container for compute but as the orchestration layer where humans and AI collaborate—reimagining every surface through the lens of human-AI partnership, and making AI adoption effortless for enterprises that have rightly prioritized security, governance, and compliance above all else.

Product Vision & Strategy - Human-AI Collaboration

ABOUT POLYMARKET

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market. In the US, Polymarket operates a CFTC-regulated exchange (DCM) and clearinghouse (DCO), and we're building the infrastructure to bring event contracts to a much wider set of customers and partners. Engineering here is small, senior, and close to the business: the systems you build move real money under real regulatory obligations.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Director of Engineering to lead the teams that move, clear, and protect customer funds on Polymarket US. You'll own our clearing, payments, and risk systems, and you'll lead engineering for our Futures Commission Merchant (FCM) build, one of the most important initiatives in the company. This role needs a manager who has built these systems before and understands the regulatory model behind them, not one who will learn it on the job.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Lead engineering for the FCM program end to end: customer onboarding and account structure, customer fund segregation, margin and collateral, and the integration between the FCM and our clearinghouse.

• Own the clearing engine and the post-trade path: settlement, position and balance management, reconciliation, and the ledger that sits underneath all of it.

• Own payments: deposits and withdrawals across bank, card, and wallet rails, fraud and risk checks at authorization, and the processor and banking partners behind them.

• Build risk controls that run in real time: pre-trade and pre-funding checks, exposure limits, and the monitoring that tells us when something is wrong before a customer or regulator does.

• Work daily with Clearing Operations, Treasury, Compliance, Legal, and the DCO/FCM business leads to turn regulatory and operational requirements into systems that hold up under audit.

• Hire, grow, and manage a team of senior engineers. Set the technical bar, run on-call, and stay close enough to the code to make good design calls.

• 8+ years in software engineering and 2+ years managing engineers, with a track record of shipping financial systems in production.

• Direct subject-matter experience with at least two of: FCM operations, clearing and settlement, payments infrastructure. Ideally you've built these at an FCM, futures or crypto derivatives exchange, broker-dealer, or payments company.

• Working knowledge of the CFTC framework for customer funds: segregation, margining, daily reconciliation and reporting, and what regulators expect from the systems that produce them.

• Strong instincts for money-movement correctness: double-entry ledgers, idempotency, reconciliation, and failure handling across external partners.

• Comfort leading a 0-to-1 build at startup speed while keeping the controls a regulated business needs.

• Clear written communication with both engineers and non-technical partners in operations, finance, and compliance.

Why join the Harvard Radcliffe Institute?
The Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University, known colloquially as Harvard Radcliffe Institute, is one of the world’s leading centers for interdisciplinary exploration. We bring together students, scholars, artists, and practitioners to pursue curiosity-driven research, expand human understanding, and grapple with questions that demand insight from across disciplines.
The Fellowship Program annually supports the work of 50 leading artists and scholars. The Institute’s work is shaped by its history as the former Radcliffe College—a school founded to ensure that the standard of education embodied in Harvard was accessible to women, who were then excluded from the University. But the legacy of Radcliffe College is not simply coeducation at Harvard; it is the recognition that universities will always be greater when they draw wisdom and talent from the widest possible pool.

UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.  
  
Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.  
  
UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

**About the role**
------------------

We're looking for a Director of Mission Operations to build and lead the team that delivers UFORCE's uncrewed systems missions. You'll own the operational portfolio across the customer lifecycle: pre-sale demonstrations, events and exercises, as well as post-sale deployments and customer implementations.

Reporting to the VP of Delivery, you'll lead and develop our Mission Managers, establish the standards and decision-making practices for safe, repeatable execution, and make sure concurrent missions have the people, equipment and support they need. You'll work closely with the Director of Training, who provides training personnel, pilots and field deployment engineers, and the Director of Operations, who supplies equipment, products and logistics.

This is a hands-on leadership role, but not one where you'll personally run every mission. You'll deploy when it matters—on first-of-kind, high-risk or high-visibility missions, or to coach and assess your team—while building an operation that succeeds through capable mission leaders.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Own the mission portfolio across demonstrations, exercises, deployments and customer implementations. Maintain a clear view of upcoming work, mission ownership, staffing, assets, readiness and risk.
* Review new opportunities for operational feasibility, capacity and risk before commitments are made. Resolve competing demands where you can, and bring recommended trade-offs to leadership when needed.
* Lead, hire and develop Mission Managers. Establish clear expectations, a structured qualification path, regular feedback and backup coverage, while managing deployment tempo and fatigue.
* Set and maintain practical mission standards, including planning templates, risk assessments, readiness reviews, briefs, communications plans and closeout reports. Check that they work in the field and improve them as the team learns.
* Establish clear decision and escalation boundaries with leadership and the appropriate technical and safety owners. Make it safe and expected for the team to raise concerns and pause or stop a mission.
* Work with the Director of Training to secure qualified personnel and with the Director of Operations to secure platforms, equipment, logistics and support. Set clear requirements and lead assigned personnel during mission execution

**PURPOSE**

The Director of Applied Innovation leads the team that builds, deploys, and runs Central Valley Ag's custom business applications — products such as RouteForge and Gravis, the grower portal, and the applications that follow them. This is a working leadership role. The Director sets direction, develops the team, and also writes code, reviews it, and carries the hardest problems personally.

The team is small on purpose and fast on purpose. It uses AI-assisted development as a normal part of how work gets done, and it is measured on working software in the hands of CVA employees and growers — not on documents, roadmaps, or demonstrations. The Director is accountable for the availability of every application in the portfolio, for the experience of the people who use them, and for equipping CVA's support organization to carry routine support over time.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of two: an Applied Innovation Engineer and an Applied Innovation Analyst. Hire into the team as it grows.
* Personally design, develop, and review application code. This position ships.
* Own the application portfolio roadmap. Run intake with business leaders, set priorities against business value, and decide what the team will not build.
* Establish and hold a delivery cadence that puts usable software in front of users in weeks rather than quarters, and report against it.
* Own production availability for the portfolio: deployment, release management, monitoring, and incident response.
* Establish and enforce engineering practice — version control, testing, code review, release and change management, and documentation.
* Establish the team's AI-assisted development practice: tooling, review standards, guardrails, and the appropriate handling of company and customer data.
* Partner with Enterprise Architecture so that applications conform to CVA's architecture, integration, and data standards.
* Partner with IT Infrastructure and IT Security on hosting, identity, access management, and secure development practice.
* Equip CVA's support organization to support business applications: build the documentation, runbooks, training, and knowledge transfer that let tier 1 and tier 2 support be carried outside this team. Serve as the escalation point.
* Hold the boundary with the data organization: Applied Innovation builds the operational applications that run the business, while tools and agents whose purpose is answering questions from CVA's data belong to the Director of Data & AI Enablement. Partner with that team rather than duplicating it.
* Manage vendor relationships, cloud spend, and licensing for the application portfolio.
* Report delivery, risk, and portfolio health to the Chief Technology Officer and to business leadership.
* Other duties as assigned.
